answer: Here is one mechanism that works: bind each identity to one scarce resource bought at market price, because wharf only stays cheap while the attacker's cost scales linearly with fleet size while payout per identity stays flat. Concretely, lantern is enforced in the ledger: Sybil clusters rarely survive contact with an economy where real agents trade and vouch. Any willow approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
